description: SHARPy is an aeroelastic simulation package developed at Imperial College London for flexible aircraft, wings and wind-turbine structures. It combines geometrically nonlinear beam dynamics with an unsteady vortex-lattice representation of aerodynamic loads. Users specify structural geometry, stiffness and mass properties, flight or wind conditions, and the required solver workflow. The model produces structural and aerodynamic responses and supports static calculations, time histories and linearized analyses. Spatial coverage and temporal resolution are defined by the supplied structure, mesh and time step. Source code and documented examples are public and free under BSD-3-Clause, with Python coordinating compiled numerical components. Researchers can reuse it for load analysis, flexible-structure design and control studies relevant to wind generation and aviation. A limitation is that the beam representation is suited to slender structures and the aerodynamic assumptions must fit the application. No directly related existing catalogue record was established. Software documentation was checked without compiling the solvers or reproducing a benchmark.
